BOWLING GREEN, Ky. – South Warren Spartans Alex Miller, Noah Rowland, Dylan Marr and Tucker Sears signed their national letters of intent to play baseball at the collegiate level.

Miller will be heading to Kentucky Wesleyan College after being a key contributor at the plate for South last season. He posted a .353 batting average and finished second on the team with 27 RBI.

His teammate Sears has also played a vital role for the Spartans both on the plate and behind it at catcher and he’ll be heading to Frontier Community College.

South Warren coaches described these athletes as never afraid to step up in competition and standing out as leaders – qualities they feel confident that they are bringing to their future team.

“ (Frontier) is getting a tough kid that’s got a lot of heart and is scrappy and will do anything the team needs,” Sears said.

“I think just working hard in general is what it takes to be a good baseball player, and I think I have that quality,” Miller said. “I think I’m just going to keep doing that. I’ve always done that my entire life from a young age, so I’m going to keep that up.”

Marr and Rowland will both be taking their talents to Rend Lake College and have seen some significant amount of time on the mound for South.

Rowland is coming off a season where he tossed a 3.93 ERA in nearly 33 innings, while Marr was more of two-way player with a 3.46 ERA in addition to 26 hits this past year.

With just one more season left to play as Spartans, Rowland and Marr spoke on what they will be taking away from their time at South Warren.

“Obviously you remember state and the big games, but you remember the camaraderie you have with the team, friendships and all that you build with them,” Marr said. “You get really tight in the locker room.”

“I’ll definitely always be a learner,” Rowland said. “I know one of my coaches said I was always asking questions, sometimes too many. I like to learn, so just being a learner is something I can take with me throughout my whole life.”
